criteria.criterion: Packaged Python is the sole runner-neutral orchestration implementation; no repository-local runner script is required.
`rebar.bridge_run(profile=..., repo_root=...)` exposes the operation through the public Python library and returns captured structured output without writing streams.
`rebar bridge run --profile ...` exposes the same operation through the installed CLI and renders captured streams once.
MCP exposes the same operation as a typed write-gated tool, blocked by read-only mode and requiring Jira-sync authorization.
The wheel contains the runner core and proves availability from pip, Homebrew wheel-backed, and MCP Registry/uvx install shapes.
Explicit `repo_root` overrides inherited `REBAR_ROOT`; installed CLI use outside a repository honors configured `REBAR_ROOT`.
All five existing provider `MODE` values remain accepted and map to the specified legacy or canonical routes.
Public help, library, MCP, schemas, and docs use `profile`; provider configuration retains `MODE` compatibility.
Direct legacy reconcile callers retain published benign results 3/4/75.
The runner translates legacy benign results to canonical 0 while preserving operational 1 and invalid-invocation 2.
Exact valid pause markers skip delivery and return success; malformed markers do not silently pause.
Every successful non-paused pass invokes strict delivery with run id, bot identity, and `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`; delivery failure returns 1 with diagnostics.
A shallow repository returns invalid invocation before reconciliation.
GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and GitLab invoke exactly `rebar bridge run`; GitHub keeps the 20-minute schedule and optional continuous redispatch.
Provider wrappers are schema-validated and their embedded shell passes the pinned ShellCheck; missing or mismatched tooling fails validation.
GitLab schema provenance records and verifies an immutable upstream revision and checksum.
Copied-workflow migration documentation requires atomic workflow and package-pin refresh, while old workflows on old pins remain supported.
Existing workflow, policy, partial-clone, identity, legacy compatibility, library, CLI, and MCP tests remain green.
